As of early 2025, the next solar eclipse is a partial solar eclipse on **September 21, 2025**, visible over remote Southern Hemisphere regions including New Zealand, Australia, Antarctica, and parts of the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans [d6][d4]. It begins at 1:29 p.m. EDT and reaches its maximum phase at 3:41 p.m. EDT, when the sun will appear as a thin crescent [d6]. Following that, the next eclipses in sequence are an annular solar eclipse on February 17, 2026, and then a total solar eclipse on August 12, 2026, visible in Greenland, Iceland, Spain, Russia, and a small area of Portugal [d2][d1]. For viewers in the contiguous United States specifically, the next total solar eclipse visible from that region will not occur until August 23, 2044 [d3].
